comparison: Perfect alignment on C35-C37 regarding D63G mutation effects. Both find the fluorescence shift and lack of functional impact supported, with peer reviewers noting this raises 'interesting questions about how this mutation enhances viral fitness.'

Perfect alignment on C38-C42 regarding thermal stability findings. Both accept DSF data showing G215C affects folded domain stability through nonlocal effects as part of comprehensive biophysical characterization.

Perfect alignment on C43-C45 regarding CD spectroscopy findings. Both accept increased helical content interpretation and attribution to L-rich region helices as part of convincing structural analysis.
Perfect alignment on C46-C49 regarding oligomerization findings. Both accept SV-AUC data showing G215C promotes higher oligomers, consistent with previous work on coiled-coil interactions.

Perfect alignment on C50-C56 regarding particle formation and epistatic effects. Both accept DLS data showing R203K/G204R disrupts phase separation and non-additive effects in Omicron. Peer reviewers describe these as 'provocative results.'

Perfect alignment on C57-C61 regarding P13L self-association. Both strongly support this novel finding. Peer reviewers highlight it as 'most notable,' noting ColabFold and sedimentation analysis suggest P13L promotes N-terminal self-association.

Perfect alignment on C62-C66 regarding LLPS modulation by mutations. Both accept optical microscopy and quantitative analysis showing differential droplet formation. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'provocative results that set the stage for in-depth analyses.'

Perfect alignment on C69-C72 regarding main conclusions. Both strongly support overarching conclusions about nonlocal effects, compensatory mechanisms, and new P13L interface. Peer reviewers describe work as providing 'new insights' with 'novel findings worthy of further exploration.'

Perfect alignment on C73-C77, C82-C83 regarding biological context of mutations. Both accept cited findings about epidemiological significance. Peer reviewers validate novelty by noting P13L's biophysical effects 'have not been previously studied.'

Perfect alignment on C28-C29 regarding variant mutations within broader spectrum. Both accept observation that variant-defining mutations fall within range of broader mutant landscape, supporting conclusions about IDR plasticity.

Strong alignment on C67-C68 regarding plasticity within constraints. OpenEval emphasizes dual observation of variation within regions and separation between regions. Alignment on functional context (C16-C18, C21). OpenEval categorizes these as established background knowledge. Peer reviewers accept functional descriptions, noting 'the central disordered linker is particularly well understood' including SR-rich phosphorylation and leucine-rich oligomerization.

Alignment on C84 regarding independent occurrence of mutations. OpenEval supports based on database analysis. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as part of manuscript's interpretation framework.
